title: Goldman Sachs to Acquire ETF Provider Neos Investments for $2.25 Billion
excerpt: The deal will make Goldman Sachs a top-eight active ETF provider globally, adding $30 billion in options-based income funds to its asset management platform.
body:
• Goldman Sachs will acquire Neos Investments for up to $2.25 billion, adding 19 systematic options-based income ETFs managing $30 billion in assets.
  • The deal, expected to close in Q1 2027, will push Goldman's active ETF assets to $80 billion and position it as a top-eight global active ETF provider.
  • This is Goldman's second major ETF acquisition in under a year, following its $2 billion purchase of Innovator Capital Management completed in April 2026.
  • Active ETFs globally now oversee $2.6 trillion, up 34.2% since the end of 2025, with first-half 2026 inflows more than double the previous record.

Goldman Sachs will acquire exchange-traded funds provider Neos Investments for as much as $2.25 billion, the investment bank announced on Tuesday, in its second major ETF deal in under a year as it pushes deeper into asset management.

Neos, which provides ETFs built on systematic options-based income strategies, managed $30 billion in assets across 19 funds as of June 30. The acquisition, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, will propel Goldman's active ETF assets to roughly $80 billion.

A Growing ETF Empire

The deal follows Goldman's $2 billion acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, which specializes in defined outcome ETFs using options-based strategies. That purchase closed in April 2026 and brought approximately $31 billion in assets and 171 ETFs into Goldman's fold.

Combined with Neos, Goldman Sachs Asset Management will oversee approximately $130 billion across its global ETF platform and rank among the top eight active ETF providers worldwide.

"Neos is highly complementary to our capabilities across buffer, managed outcome and income strategies."

— David Solomon, CEO, Goldman Sachs

Troy Cates and Garrett Paolella, who co-founded Neos in 2022, will join Goldman Sachs Asset Management as partners when the deal completes.

Why Options-Based ETFs

Demand for options-based ETF strategies has surged as institutions seek to hedge portfolios with investments that help cushion drawdown risk in volatile markets. These funds use options contracts to generate income or provide defined levels of downside protection, offering an alternative to traditional bond allocations.

The broader active ETF segment has grown rapidly. Active ETFs globally now oversee $2.6 trillion at the end of June, an increase of 34.2% since the end of 2025, according to data from ETFGI. During the first half of 2026, active ETFs attracted $500.1 billion in inflows globally — more than double the previous full-year record of $266.5 billion set in 2025.

Goldman's Asset Management Pivot

Goldman has pursued acquisitions in the actively managed ETF segment as part of a broader strategy to diversify beyond its traditional strengths in trading and investment banking. Asset management generates more predictable, fee-based revenue than the cyclical dealmaking and trading businesses that have historically defined the firm.

The push into ETFs also reflects a structural shift in the investment industry. Investors have steadily moved assets from traditional mutual funds into the ETF wrapper, which offers lower costs, greater tax efficiency, and intraday liquidity. Active ETFs — which combine professional portfolio management with the ETF structure — have emerged as the fastest-growing segment of this trend.

What's Next

The Neos acquisition is subject to regulatory approval and customary closing conditions. Goldman has not disclosed the exact breakdown of cash and equity in the consideration, though the $2.25 billion figure is subject to the achievement of certain performance targets.

For Goldman, the question now shifts to integration. Managing a combined active ETF platform spanning buffer, defined outcome, and options-based income strategies across hundreds of products will test the firm's ability to deliver on the scale advantages these acquisitions are designed to create.
nri_angle: Goldman Sachs's rapid expansion in ETFs reshapes the investment landscape for retail and institutional investors evaluating options-based income strategies.
